title: Codex Ultimus: Refolded Wrong
statement: Lumen unfolded the codex flat and everyone since has written on it. I folded it back up, and I folded it wrong. The octavo has eight panels and I put them back in the wrong order, some upside down, so the dawn runs in four directions at once, the bright circle where the seal was is cut into quarters that no longer meet, and the seal itself is split between two panels on opposite sides of the sheet. One panel came back a hot pink that was never in the letter, because when you refold something there is always a face you have not seen before. The creases are the only things in the right place. A letter folded wrong is still a letter; it is just addressed to someone who reads differently.
process: I kept the parent's full composition as a single scene, its dawn gradient, creases, threshold circle, ghost row and seal exactly, then divided the sheet into the eight octavo panels and redrew each panel with a different panel of the scene inside it, some rotated a half turn, using clip paths. One panel is replaced with flat pink; the crease lines are drawn on top in their original positions.
